autogenerate_revision_name.description:
If set to 'true', the revision name (template.metadata.name) will be omitted and
autogenerated by Cloud Run. This cannot be set to 'true' while 'template.metadata.name'
is also set.
(For legacy support, if 'template.metadata.name' is unset in state while
this field is set to false, the revision name will still autogenerate.)
autogenerate_revision_name.rationale: Revision name generation is operational and does not directly affect access, networking, encryption, or secret handling.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

location.description: The location of the cloud run instance. eg us-central1
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

name.description:
Name must be unique within a Google Cloud project and region.
Is required when creating resources. Name is primarily intended
for creation idempotence and configuration definition. Cannot be updated.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/names/#names
name.rationale: The service name is mainly used for identification and does not directly control access, networking, encryption, or runtime security.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Identifier of the GCP project hosting the service. It is a reference/identifier; constraining it would require knowing each team's approved project, which is overreaching for a generic policy.

metadata.description:
Metadata associated with this Service, including name, namespace, labels,
and annotations.

metadata.annotations.description:
Annotations is a key value map stored with a resource that
may be set by external tools to store and retrieve arbitrary metadata.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/annotations

**Note**: The Cloud Run API may add additional annotations that were not provided in your config.
If terraform plan shows a diff where a server-side annotation is added, you can add it to your config
or apply the lifecycle.ignore_changes rule to the metadata.0.annotations field.

Annotations with 'run.googleapis.com/' and 'autoscaling.knative.dev' are restricted. Use the following annotation
keys to configure features on a Service:

- 'run.googleapis.com/binary-authorization-breakglass' sets the [Binary Authorization breakglass](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/run/deploy#--breakglass).
- 'run.googleapis.com/binary-authorization' sets the [Binary Authorization](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/run/deploy#--binary-authorization).
- 'run.googleapis.com/client-name' sets the client name calling the Cloud Run API.
- 'run.googleapis.com/custom-audiences' sets the [custom audiences](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/alpha/run/deploy#--add-custom-audiences)
  that can be used in the audience field of ID token for authenticated requests.
- 'run.googleapis.com/description' sets a user defined description for the Service.
- 'run.googleapis.com/ingress' sets the [ingress settings](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/run/deploy#--ingress)
  for the Service. For example, '"run.googleapis.com/ingress" = "all"'.
- 'run.googleapis.com/launch-stage' sets the [launch stage](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/troubleshooting#launch-stage-validation)
  when a preview feature is used. For example, '"run.googleapis.com/launch-stage": "BETA"'
- 'run.googleapis.com/minScale' sets the [minimum number of container instances](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/run/deploy#--min) of the Service.
- 'run.googleapis.com/scalingMode' sets the type of scaling mode for the service. The supported values for scaling mode are "manual" and "automatic". If not provided, it defaults to "automatic".
- 'run.googleapis.com/manualInstanceCount' sets the total instance count for the service in manual scaling mode. This number of instances is divided among all revisions with specified traffic based on the percent of traffic they are receiving.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the annotations present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_annotations' for all of the annotations present on the resource.
metadata.annotations.rationale: Annotations can control ingress, Binary Authorization, custom audiences, VPC access, Cloud SQL, encryption, and scaling.

metadata.labels.description:
Map of string keys and values that can be used to organize and categorize
(scope and select) objects. May match selectors of replication controllers
and routes.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
metadata.labels.rationale: Free-form key/value labels for organization and cost tracking. Labels are descriptive metadata and do not control access, networking, or encryption, so they are not a security policy target.

metadata.namespace.description:
In Cloud Run the namespace must be equal to either the
project ID or project number.
metadata.namespace.rationale: For Cloud Run the namespace equals the project ID/number. It is an identifier referencing the host project; a platform policy cannot know the approved project for an arbitrary team, so enforcing a specific value is overreaching.

template.description:
template holds the latest specification for the Revision to
be stamped out. The template references the container image, and may also
include labels and annotations that should be attached to the Revision.
To correlate a Revision, and/or to force a Revision to be created when the
spec doesn't otherwise change, a nonce label may be provided in the
template metadata. For more details, see:
https://github.com/knative/serving/blob/main/docs/client-conventions.md#associate-modifications-with-revisions

Cloud Run does not currently support referencing a build that is
responsible for materializing the container image from source.

template.metadata.description:
Optional metadata for this Revision, including labels and annotations.
Name will be generated by the Configuration. To set minimum instances
for this revision, use the "autoscaling.knative.dev/minScale" annotation
key. To set maximum instances for this revision, use the
"autoscaling.knative.dev/maxScale" annotation key. To set Cloud SQL
connections for the revision, use the "run.googleapis.com/cloudsql-instances"
annotation key.

template.metadata.annotations.description:
Annotations is a key value map stored with a resource that
may be set by external tools to store and retrieve arbitrary metadata.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/annotations

**Note**: The Cloud Run API may add additional annotations that were not provided in your config.
If terraform plan shows a diff where a server-side annotation is added, you can add it to your config
or apply the lifecycle.ignore_changes rule to the metadata.0.annotations field.

Annotations with 'run.googleapis.com/' and 'autoscaling.knative.dev' are restricted. Use the following annotation
keys to configure features on a Revision template:

- 'autoscaling.knative.dev/maxScale' sets the [maximum number of container
  instances](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/run/deploy#--max-instances) of the Revision to run.
- 'autoscaling.knative.dev/minScale' sets the [minimum number of container
  instances](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/run/deploy#--min-instances) of the Revision to run.
- 'run.googleapis.com/client-name' sets the client name calling the Cloud Run API.
- 'run.googleapis.com/cloudsql-instances' sets the [Cloud SQL
  instances](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/run/deploy#--add-cloudsql-instances) the Revision connects to.
- 'run.googleapis.com/cpu-throttling' sets whether to throttle the CPU when the container is not actively serving
  requests. See https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/run/deploy#--[no-]cpu-throttling.
- 'run.googleapis.com/encryption-key-shutdown-hours' sets the number of hours to wait before an automatic shutdown
  server after CMEK key revocation is detected.
- 'run.googleapis.com/encryption-key' sets the [CMEK key](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/securing/using-cmek)
  reference to encrypt the container with.
- 'run.googleapis.com/execution-environment' sets the [execution
  environment](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/run/deploy#--execution-environment)
  where the application will run.
- 'run.googleapis.com/post-key-revocation-action-type' sets the
  [action type](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/run/deploy#--post-key-revocation-action-type)
  after CMEK key revocation.
- 'run.googleapis.com/secrets' sets a list of key-value pairs to set as
  [secrets](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/secrets#yaml).
- 'run.googleapis.com/sessionAffinity' sets whether to enable
  [session affinity](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/beta/run/deploy#--[no-]session-affinity)
  for connections to the Revision.
- 'run.googleapis.com/startup-cpu-boost' sets whether to allocate extra CPU to containers on startup.
  See https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/run/deploy#--[no-]cpu-boost.
- 'run.googleapis.com/network-interfaces' sets [Direct VPC egress](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/vpc-direct-vpc#yaml)
  for the Revision.
- 'run.googleapis.com/vpc-access-connector' sets a [VPC connector](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/connecting-vpc#terraform_1)
  for the Revision.
- 'run.googleapis.com/vpc-access-egress' sets the outbound traffic to send through the VPC connector for this resource.
  See https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/run/deploy#--vpc-egress.
- 'run.googleapis.com/gpu-zonal-redundancy-disabled' sets
  [GPU zonal redundancy](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/gpu-zonal-redundancy) for the Revision.
- 'run.googleapis.com/health-check-disabled' disabled health checking containers during deployment.

template.metadata.labels.description:
Map of string keys and values that can be used to organize and categorize
(scope and select) objects.

template.metadata.name.description:
Name must be unique within a Google Cloud project and region.
Is required when creating resources. Name is primarily intended
for creation idempotence and configuration definition. Cannot be updated.

template.metadata.namespace.description:
In Cloud Run the namespace must be equal to either the
project ID or project number. It will default to the resource's project.

template.spec.description: RevisionSpec holds the desired state of the Revision (from the client).

template.spec.container_concurrency.description:
ContainerConcurrency specifies the maximum allowed in-flight (concurrent)
requests per container of the Revision. If not specified or 0, defaults to 80 when
requested CPU >= 1 and defaults to 1 when requested CPU < 1.
template.spec.container_concurrency.rationale: Sets the maximum concurrent requests per container instance. This is a performance/capacity tuning choice; there is no generic secure value to enforce across all teams, so it matches no security archetype.

template.spec.node_selector.description:
Node Selector describes the hardware requirements of the resources.
Use the following node selector keys to configure features on a Revision:
  - 'run.googleapis.com/accelerator' sets the [type of GPU](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/gpu) required by the Revision to run.
template.spec.node_selector.rationale: Node selector is mainly used for hardware selection and was not treated as a core Cloud Run security control in this policy set.

template.spec.service_account_name.description:
Email address of the IAM service account associated with the revision of the
service. The service account represents the identity of the running revision,
and determines what permissions the revision has. If not provided, the revision
will use the project's default service account.
template.spec.service_account_name.rationale: The service account controls the permissions available to the running service. A dedicated least-privilege account should be used.

template.spec.timeout_seconds.description: TimeoutSeconds holds the max duration the instance is allowed for responding to a request.

template.spec.containers.description: Containers defines the unit of execution for this Revision.

template.spec.containers.args.description:
Arguments to the entrypoint.
The docker image's CMD is used if this is not provided.
template.spec.containers.args.rationale: Container arguments are application-specific and were not treated as a general security policy in this scope.

template.spec.containers.command.description:
Entrypoint array. Not executed within a shell.
The docker image's ENTRYPOINT is used if this is not provided.
template.spec.containers.command.rationale: Entrypoint command is application-specific and was not treated as a general Cloud Run security baseline policy.

template.spec.containers.image.description:
Docker image name. This is most often a reference to a container located
in the container registry, such as gcr.io/cloudrun/hello
template.spec.containers.image.rationale: Only approved image registries should be used to reduce the risk of deploying untrusted or malicious images.

template.spec.containers.working_dir.description:
Container's working directory.
If not specified, the container runtime's default will be used, which
might be configured in the container image.
template.spec.containers.working_dir.rationale: Working directory is deprecated and not supported by the Cloud Run API.

template.spec.containers.env.description: List of environment variables to set in the container.

template.spec.containers.env.value_from.description: Source for the environment variable's value. Only supports secret_key_ref.

template.spec.containers.env.value_from..description: Selects a key (version) of a secret in Secret Manager.

A Cloud Secret Manager secret version. Must be 'latest' for the latest
version or an integer for a specific version.

The name of the secret in Cloud Secret Manager. By default, the secret is assumed to be in the same project.
If the secret is in another project, you must define an alias.
An alias definition has the form:
{alias}:projects/{project-id|project-number}/secrets/{secret-name}.
If multiple alias definitions are needed, they must be separated by commas.
The alias definitions must be set on the run.googleapis.com/secrets annotation.

template.spec.containers.env_from.description:
List of sources to populate environment variables in the container.
All invalid keys will be reported as an event when the container is starting.
When a key exists in multiple sources, the value associated with the last source will
take precedence. Values defined by an Env with a duplicate key will take
precedence.

template.spec.containers.env_from.prefix.description: An optional identifier to prepend to each key in the ConfigMap.
template.spec.containers.env_from.prefix.rationale: Prefix is mainly a naming convenience and does not directly control access or secret exposure.

template.spec.containers.env_from.config.description: Specify whether the ConfigMap must be defined

template.spec.containers.env_from.secret.description: Specify whether the Secret must be defined

template.spec.containers.liveness_probe.description: Periodic probe of container liveness. Container will be restarted if the probe fails.

template.spec.containers.liveness_probe..description:
Minimum consecutive failures for the probe to be considered failed after
having succeeded. Defaults to 3. Minimum value is 1.

Number of seconds after the container has started before the probe is
initiated.
Defaults to 0 seconds. Minimum value is 0. Maximum value is 3600.

How often (in seconds) to perform the probe.
Default to 10 seconds. Minimum value is 1. Maximum value is 3600.

Number of seconds after which the probe times out.
Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1. Maximum value is 3600.
Must be smaller than period_seconds.
GRPC specifies an action involving a GRPC port.

Port number to access on the container. Number must be in the range 1 to 65535.
If not specified, defaults to the same value as container.ports[0].containerPort.

The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest
(see https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/doc/health-checking.md).
If this is not specified, the default behavior is defined by gRPC.
HttpGet specifies the http request to perform.
Path to access on the HTTP server. If set, it should not be empty string.

Port number to access on the container. Number must be in the range 1 to 65535.
If not specified, defaults to the same value as container.ports[0].containerPort.
Custom headers to set in the request. HTTP allows repeated headers.

template.spec.containers.ports.description: List of open ports in the container.

template.spec.containers.ports.container.description: Port number the container listens on. This must be a valid port number (between 1 and 65535). Defaults to "8080".
template.spec.containers.ports.container.rationale: Declares the port the container listens on so Cloud Run can route requests. It only sets where the app listens behind Cloud Run's managed frontend; it does not open the port to the internet, so constraining it does not improve security.

template.spec.containers.ports.name.description: If specified, used to specify which protocol to use. Allowed values are "http1" (HTTP/1) and "h2c" (HTTP/2 end-to-end). Defaults to "http1".

template.spec.containers.ports.protocol.description: Protocol for port. Must be "TCP". Defaults to "TCP".
template.spec.containers.ports.protocol.rationale: Cloud Run requires TCP, so this was not treated as a custom security policy in this scope.

template.spec.containers.readiness_probe.description:
Minimum consecutive failures for the probe to be considered failed after
having succeeded. Defaults to 3.

How often (in seconds) to perform the probe.
Default to 10 seconds.

Minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after having failed.
Defaults to 2.

Number of seconds after which the probe times out.
Defaults to 1 second. Must be smaller than period_seconds.
GRPC specifies an action involving a GRPC port.

Port number to access on the container. Number must be in the range 1 to 65535.
If not specified, defaults to the same value as container.ports[0].containerPort.

The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest
(see https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/doc/health-checking.md).
If this is not specified, the default behavior is defined by gRPC.
HttpGet specifies the http request to perform.
Path to access on the HTTP server. If set, it should not be empty string.

Port number to access on the container. Number must be in the range 1 to 65535.
If not specified, defaults to the same value as container.ports[0].containerPort.

template.spec.containers.resources.description: Compute Resources required by this container. Used to set values such as max memory

template.spec.containers.resources.limit.description:
Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed.
CPU Limit details:
- For fractional CPU values (e.g. '0.5', '0.75', min '0.08') are also supported.
- CPU allocation must comply with memory limits and concurrency rules described in:
  https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/cpu
The values of the map is string form of the 'quantity' k8s type:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource/quantity.go
template.spec.containers.resources.limit.rationale: Sets per-container CPU/memory resource limits. This is a capacity/cost tuning choice; there is no generic secure value to enforce across teams, so it is not a platform security policy target.

template.spec.containers.resources.reque.description:
Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required.
If Requests is omitted for a container, it defaults to Limits if that is
explicitly specified, otherwise to an implementation-defined value.
The values of the map is string form of the 'quantity' k8s type:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/resource/quantity.go
template.spec.containers.resources.reque.rationale: Sets per-container CPU/memory resource requests. This is a capacity/cost tuning choice with no generic secure value, so it is not a platform security policy target.

template.spec.containers.startup_probe.description:
Startup probe of application within the container.
All other probes are disabled if a startup probe is provided, until it
succeeds. Container will not be added to service endpoints if the probe fails.

template.spec.containers.startup_probe.f.description:
Minimum consecutive failures for the probe to be considered failed after
having succeeded. Defaults to 3. Minimum value is 1.

template.spec.containers.startup_probe.i.description:
Number of seconds after the container has started before the probe is
initiated.
Defaults to 0 seconds. Minimum value is 0. Maximum value is 240.

template.spec.containers.startup_probe.p.description:
How often (in seconds) to perform the probe.
Default to 10 seconds. Minimum value is 1. Maximum value is 240.

template.spec.containers.startup_probe.t.description:
Number of seconds after which the probe times out.
Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1. Maximum value is 3600.
Must be smaller than periodSeconds.

template.spec.containers.startup_probe.g.description: GRPC specifies an action involving a GRPC port.

Port number to access on the container. Number must be in the range 1 to 65535.
If not specified, defaults to the same value as container.ports[0].containerPort.

The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest
(see https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/doc/health-checking.md).
If this is not specified, the default behavior is defined by gRPC.

template.spec.containers.startup_probe.h.description: HttpGet specifies the http request to perform.
Path to access on the HTTP server. If set, it should not be empty string.

Port number to access on the container. Number must be in the range 1 to 65535.
If not specified, defaults to the same value as container.ports[0].containerPort.
Custom headers to set in the request. HTTP allows repeated headers.

template.spec.containers.startup_probe.t.description: TcpSocket specifies an action involving a TCP port.

Port number to access on the container. Number must be in the range 1 to 65535.
If not specified, defaults to the same value as container.ports[0].containerPort.

template.spec.containers.volume_mounts.description:
Volume to mount into the container's filesystem.
Only supports SecretVolumeSources.

template.spec.containers.volume_mounts.m.description:
Path within the container at which the volume should be mounted.  Must
not contain ':'.
template.spec.containers.volume_mounts.m.rationale: Specifies the in-container filesystem path where a volume is mounted. The path is an app-specific layout detail visible only inside the container; constraining it does not change who can access the secret and matches no archetype.

template.spec.containers.volume_mounts.n.description: This must match the Name of a Volume.

template.spec.containers.volume_mounts.s.description: Path within the volume from which the container's volume should be mounted.

template.spec.volumes.description: Volume represents a named volume in a container.

template.spec.volumes.csi.description: A filesystem specified by the Container Storage Interface (CSI).

template.spec.volumes.csi.driver.description:
Unique name representing the type of file system to be created. Cloud Run supports the following values:
  * gcsfuse.run.googleapis.com: Mount a Google Cloud Storage bucket using GCSFuse. This driver requires the
    run.googleapis.com/execution-environment annotation to be unset or set to "gen2"
template.spec.volumes.csi.driver.rationale: Names the CSI driver backing a volume (e.g. the GCS Fuse driver). This identifies which managed storage driver to mount and is a reference/identifier rather than a security control; enforcing a specific driver name is not a platform security guarantee.

template.spec.volumes.csi.read_only.description: If true, all mounts created from this volume will be read-only.

template.spec.volumes.csi.volume_attribu.description:
Driver-specific attributes. The following options are supported for available drivers:
  * gcsfuse.run.googleapis.com
    * bucketName: The name of the Cloud Storage Bucket that backs this volume. The Cloud Run Service identity must have access to this bucket.
template.spec.volumes.csi.volume_attribu.rationale: Free-form driver-specific attributes (e.g. the bucket name for a CSI volume). These reference other resources and are arbitrary key/values; we do not constrain references to other resources and a generic policy cannot pin specific bucket names.

template.spec.volumes.empty_dir.description: Ephemeral storage which can be backed by real disks (HD, SSD), network storage or memory (i.e. tmpfs). For now only in memory (tmpfs) is supported. It is ephemeral in the sense that when the sandbox is taken down, the data is destroyed with it (it does not persist across sandbox runs).

template.spec.volumes.empty_dir.medium.description: The medium on which the data is stored. The default is "" which means to use the node's default medium. Must be an empty string (default) or Memory.
template.spec.volumes.empty_dir.medium.rationale: Storage medium is operational and workload-specific.

template.spec.volumes.empty_dir.size_lim.description: Limit on the storage usable by this EmptyDir volume. The size limit is also applicable for memory medium. The maximum usage on memory medium EmptyDir would be the minimum value between the SizeLimit specified here and the sum of memory limits of all containers in a pod. This field's values are of the 'Quantity' k8s type: https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/common-definitions/quantity/. The default is nil which means that the limit is undefined. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volumes/#emptydir.
template.spec.volumes.empty_dir.size_lim.rationale: Size limits can help control resource use, but this was not included in the implemented high-impact policy set.

template.spec.volumes.nfs.description:
A filesystem backed by a Network File System share. This filesystem requires the
run.googleapis.com/execution-environment annotation to be unset or set to "gen2"

template.spec.volumes.nfs.path.description: Path exported by the NFS server

template.spec.volumes.nfs.read_only.description: If true, mount the NFS volume as read only in all mounts. Defaults to false.

template.spec.volumes.nfs.server.description: IP address or hostname of the NFS server
template.spec.volumes.nfs.server.rationale: The hostname/IP of the NFS server backing the volume. This is a reference to external storage; a generic policy cannot know a team's approved NFS endpoints, so enforcing specific values is overreaching.

template.spec.volumes.secret.description:
The secret's value will be presented as the content of a file whose
name is defined in the item path. If no items are defined, the name of
the file is the secret_name.

template.spec.volumes.secret.default_mod.description:
Mode bits to use on created files by default. Must be a value between 0000
and 0777. Defaults to 0644. Directories within the path are not affected by
this setting. This might be in conflict with other options that affect the
file mode, like fsGroup, and the result can be other mode bits set.
template.spec.volumes.secret.default_mod.rationale: Mounted secrets should use restrictive file permissions to reduce accidental exposure.

template.spec.volumes.secret.secret_name.description:
The name of the secret in Cloud Secret Manager. By default, the secret
is assumed to be in the same project.
If the secret is in another project, you must define an alias.
An alias definition has the form:
{alias}:projects/{project-id|project-number}/secrets/{secret-name}.
If multiple alias definitions are needed, they must be separated by
commas.
The alias definitions must be set on the run.googleapis.com/secrets
annotation.
template.spec.volumes.secret.secret_name.rationale: Identifier referencing the Secret Manager secret to mount. This points at another resource; we do not constrain which secret a team references, and a generic policy cannot know approved secret names.

template.spec.volumes.secret.items.description:
If unspecified, the volume will expose a file whose name is the
secret_name.
If specified, the key will be used as the version to fetch from Cloud
Secret Manager and the path will be the name of the file exposed in the
volume. When items are defined, they must specify a key and a path.

template.spec.volumes.secret.items.key.description:
The Cloud Secret Manager secret version.
Can be 'latest' for the latest value or an integer for a specific version.

template.spec.volumes.secret.items.mode.description:
Mode bits to use on this file, must be a value between 0000 and 0777. If
not specified, the volume defaultMode will be used. This might be in
conflict with other options that affect the file mode, like fsGroup, and
the result can be other mode bits set.
template.spec.volumes.secret.items.mode.rationale: Secret item files should use restrictive permissions to prevent unnecessary access.

template.spec.volumes.secret.items.path.description:
The relative path of the file to map the key to.
May not be an absolute path.
May not contain the path element '..'.
May not start with the string '..'.

traffic.description:
Traffic specifies how to distribute traffic over a collection of Knative Revisions
and Configurations

traffic.latest_revision.description:
LatestRevision may be optionally provided to indicate that the latest ready
Revision of the Configuration should be used for this traffic target. When
provided LatestRevision must be true if RevisionName is empty; it must be
false when RevisionName is non-empty.
traffic.latest_revision.rationale: Boolean choosing whether a traffic split targets the latest revision or a pinned one. This is a deployment/release-management choice with no generic secure direction, so it matches no security archetype.

traffic.percent.description: Percent specifies percent of the traffic to this Revision or Configuration.
traffic.percent.rationale: The percentage of traffic routed to a given revision. This is a release/traffic-splitting choice; the API already validates the range and there is no generic secure value to enforce, so it matches no archetype.

traffic.revision_name.description: RevisionName of a specific revision to which to send this portion of traffic.
traffic.revision_name.rationale: Revision name is mainly operational unless a separate approved revision naming standard is enforced.

traffic.tag.description: Tag is optionally used to expose a dedicated url for referencing this target exclusively.
traffic.tag.rationale: Traffic tags are mainly used for routing and testing and do not directly control core security settings.
